payload.data: March 1938. Japan's armies drive down the Tianjin–Pukou railway toward Xuzhou. In the way, round Tengxian, stand the Sichuan troops of Sun Zhen's 22nd Group Army: tired men, a third of them with no rifle, only grenades.
04:00, 14 March: the Seya Detachment, a brigade of Isogai's 10th Division, attacks in three columns: the 10th Infantry on the right, the guns down the railway, the 63rd Infantry on the left.
11:00: the 63rd takes Xiangcheng, headquarters of the 125th Division.
On the right the 10th breaks the 370th Brigade at Shiqiang. At 19:00 the brigade falls back on Dawu, west of Tengxian.
18:10: the 63rd enters Jiehe village, astride the railway. The Chinese line from Jiehe to Longshan holds on into the next day.
10:30, 15 March, at Jiehe: Seya does not go straight down the railway. He sends the detachment round the east of Tengxian, by Dongguo and Wangmiao, to attack the city from the east.
The Japanese records route the swing far to the east, by Dongguo and Wangmiao; Chinese accounts have its van at Longyangdian, north-east of the city.
At Chengtou the Japanese light armour scatters Wang Wenzhen's 731st Regiment.
damaged
Wang Mingzhang is ordered to hold Tengxian three days for Tang Enbo's corps. He has one regiment and no heavy weapons. Sun Zhen: "That is my order; if it is not held, that is on you."
Yan Yi's battalion reaches the city at 17:00 and takes the east suburb; Zhang Xuanwu's 727th Regiment comes in at dusk, and Zhang takes command of the walls.
The 41st Army's Special Service Battalion arrives by train from Lincheng and holds the south wall. About 2,500 men are in the city; fewer than 2,000 are fighting troops.
Dawn, 16 March. Patrols report the city lightly held, so the 10th Regiment attacks with just five companies. From Xiacun its commander sees a Nazi flag over the German mission inside the walls.
Japanese records are usually in Tokyo time, but this regiment's sunrise and dusk fit local time; the replay reads its times as local.
10:20: eight field guns go into position at Xiacun, 2 km south-east of the walls. Their reach covers the city many times over.
11:00: a Chinese armoured train with 75 mm guns runs south from the station, firing; the field guns duel with it for ten minutes.
11:15: the heavy battalion ranges on the east suburb's gate. Its first round hits.
Whether the heavy battalion's twelve guns were 15 cm or 10.5 cm howitzers is disputed; the replay draws the 15 cm Type 4's 8.8 km range.
Noon: the 3rd Company's assault stops 50 m short of the suburb wall. The guns are told to make a breach first.
No Chinese 15 cm howitzer fired at Tengxian: the 10th Artillery's sFH 18/32L came with Tang Enbo's corps and first fired at Taierzhuang, on 27 or 28 March.
destroyed
14:15: through the breach the 3rd Company takes a corner of the east suburb. Grenades keep it there.
Chinese accounts have the Japanese who broke into the east suburb thrown out at dusk; the Japanese report has them holding a corner of it all night.
18:40, under a full moon: the 3rd Battalion breaks into the south suburb.
21:00: Wang gives up the outer positions. At midnight the remnants of the 370th and 372nd Brigades come in by the west gate.

07:30, 17 March: the guns open again, now with the China Garrison's modern Type 96 15 cm howitzers. At 08:30 breaching fire begins: 40 m south of the east gate, and 20 m west of the south-east corner.
damaged
Fifty rounds nearly make the east breach. The city burns, and a south wind blows the smoke north over the defenders.
10:00: a Japanese observer fights his way up the Longquan pagoda, 30 m above the city, and directs the guns.
Noon: Wang's last telegram to Sun Zhen: resolved "to fight to the death, to repay the nation and your trust".
13:00: Colonel Akashiba is grazed by a sniper. He stays in command.
14:30: the 10th's 2nd Battalion arrives and is sent to the station, to shut the way out west.
The 3rd Battalion's assault on the south breach is thrown back by grenades. At 16:05 it is on the wall, and fights west along it.
damaged
damaged
The west gate falls at about 17:00. Wang and his staff are let down from the north-west corner, to reach the troops at the station.
destroyed
destroyed
In the moat outside the west gate, machine guns on the gate tower cut down Wang Mingzhang, his chief of staff Zhao Weibin and some ten others.
Accounts of Wang Mingzhang's death differ in time and place; most put it at dusk in the moat outside the west gate, under fire from the gate tower.
damaged
Five or six hundred men who get out westward are caught at the station by the 2nd Battalion. Outside the north gate the 124th Division's chief of staff, Zou Shaomeng, is shot.
21:00: some two hundred men of the 727th open the walled-up north gate and break out.
destroyed
destroyed
21:40: the 1st Battalion is over the east wall. By 23:00 it holds the north gate.
destroyed
destroyed
18 March: the city is cleared house by house; by 14:00 it is over. Li Zongren later: without Tengxian's hard defence there would have been no victory at Taierzhuang.
18 March. From Lincheng the Seya Detachment sends two forces on: one south to Hanzhuang on the Grand Canal, one east along the branch railway to Yixian.
19 March, 13:00: the right force takes Hanzhuang north of the canal. Across the water stand about 10,000 Chinese.
At Yixian the gates will not break. After dark the men climb a human ladder through a hole above the south gate; by 00:30 the town is theirs.
Chinese accounts have Yixian fall on the evening of 18 March; the Japanese report has it taken after dark on the 19th.
Tang Enbo's 20th Army Corps gives way before them and draws off into the hills to the east, to fall on the Japanese flank later.
22 March: the 31st Division of Sun Lianzhong's 2nd Group Army takes over Taierzhuang. Chi Fengcheng puts a regiment in the walled town and another forward at Beiluo.
The 63rd's main body marches from Lincheng to Yixian.

23 March: from Yixian a battalion of the 63rd Infantry and one field battery set out to take Taierzhuang and hold the Grand Canal. At 09:00 the 31st Division's cavalry meets them at Kangzhuang; by dusk they have fought through to Beiluo.
24 March: the battalion comes down past Liujiahu and by noon is 200 m from the town's brick wall.
16:15: its guns open two breaches west of the north gate and the companies charge. About ten men get in and are cut off.
By night the battalion is out of ammunition and surrounded outside the north gate. It has lost about a hundred men.
25 March, 08:00: a Chinese armoured train runs north from the station and fires its gun on the Japanese.
The China Garrison's two Type 96 15 cm howitzers, the most modern Japanese guns here, come down by lorry from Lincheng.
16:00: the Japanese report more than ten Chinese guns at the foot of the hills south of the canal, shelling them so hard they cannot move by day.
17:30: from Liujiahu the Type 96 howitzers open fire.
At night the Chinese attack the Japanese batteries again and again; the gunners fight them off with rifles and fire at point-blank range.
26 March: the first company of the 2nd Field Heavy Artillery's Type 4 15 cm howitzers reaches Liujiahu after dark.
27 March, 06:00: every gun opens on the north wall. At 07:50 the battalion breaks into the north-east corner and raises its flag.
The 63rd's main body comes down from Yixian with the rest of the heavy artillery and a company of tanks.
The tanks charge the north-west corner. Two are destroyed and three break down.
damaged
15:40: inside the town Wang Guanwu leads a counter-attack and sets fire to the temple and blockhouses where the Japanese hold out.
Chinese accounts tell of a two-hour artillery duel on 27 March; the Japanese report records only Chinese shells on Liujiahu that evening.
28 March, 06:40: as the heavy guns range on the north-west corner, Chinese guns answer from the hills south of the canal. Their first rounds fall 100 m behind the battery.
The Japanese count at least 24 or 25 Chinese guns. They take those in the hills for field guns, those by the town for mountain guns and mortars.
Short of shells, and under the Chinese guns themselves, the Japanese batteries cannot give the infantry enough support.
damaged
19:25: after two breaching shoots by the Type 96, the 11th Company storms the north-west corner.
Chinese accounts say a special company of 72 men retook the Wenchang pavilion that night; the Japanese report keeps a foothold in the corner until 31 March.
damaged
29 March, 11:10: Chinese shells set the Type 96 company's lorries on fire. Thirteen men are killed or wounded, and nearly all its vehicles are lost.
damaged
Moved back to Liujiahu, the Type 96 hunts the Chinese batteries east of the town.
damaged

30 March. The Japanese hold the town's north-east and north-west corners and their guns stand round Liujiahu. South of the canal the Chinese 10th Artillery has brought two German 15 cm sFH 18/32L howitzers, whose 15 km outranges every Japanese gun here.
No record says where the two Chinese 15 cm howitzers stood. The replay puts them south of Xiongshan, where the Japanese thought they were, beyond the reach of every Japanese gun.
On the map each battery's reach is drawn as a fan. A Japanese gunner later wrote: "a mere two Rheinmetalls completely suppressed our whole artillery".
03:00: about a thousand Chinese come north from the station along the railway against the Japanese reserve south of Sanlizhuang.
03:30: they reach the 2nd Heavy Company's guns north of Sanlizhuang and are driven off by fire at point-blank range.
06:00: Chinese guns towards Zhaocun shell the Japanese field guns; the field guns hit two and drive off the other two.
damaged
The Type 96 company's two modern 15 cm howitzers search the villages east of the town.
17:30: a Chinese night attack forms east of Mengzhuang; the heavy guns break it up.
In the night a Chinese armoured train comes into the station from south of the canal.
06:20: the Japanese guns are ordered onto it.
31 March: the Type 96 company opens on the town's west half.
11:14: nearly all the Japanese artillery, fifteen guns, concentrates on the town, the first of four times before 14:40.
At once more than ten Chinese guns answer on the Japanese batteries at Liujiahu and Sanlizhuang.
15:05: a Chinese battery is found at Canglangmiao, east of the town; it moves on.
15:46: 15 cm-class rounds land on the 3rd Heavy Company and knock out a Type 4 howitzer: the first the Japanese have taken in the battle. They cannot find the guns.
Chinese accounts have the 15 cm guns duelling from 27 March; the Japanese record their first 15 cm-class rounds at 15:46 on 31 March.
damaged
16:15: the Type 96 company fires on a battery it has found at Hanshan.
At 17:12 the China Garrison's independent field-gun company had reported all four of its guns knocked out by Chinese fire.
20:00: under the heavy guns' cover the 11th Company gives up its foothold at the town's north-west corner.
1 April, 01:00: the 10th Field Artillery's commander will not attack under "a superior enemy artillery that has completed its preparations". The attack is put off.
15 cm rounds now fall on Liujiahu and Sanlizhuang five times through the day. The Japanese think they come from towards Xiongshan, but never find the guns.
17:25: the Type 96 company silences guns south of the station.
"Throughout the campaign our artillery hunted the Rheinmetall as its sworn enemy but never caught it" (Ohashi): on retreat the Chinese always got these guns away first.
